other_restrictions.requirement: The general duty to take all reasonable steps to protect under-eighteens informs the whole decision and is not discharged by clearing the clock. Noted because the single-event description means the reasonable-steps question cannot be answered on the asset as a whole.

decisions.axis_note: The rating does not give the hours, and this case is the exact trap: the certificate is 15, the watershed is 21:00, and the two have nothing to do with each other. The hour comes from o1 - clearly depicted intercourse - running into UK-SEX-004 and UK-SCH-002. The certificate's only role is evidential, feeding UK-FLM-010, where the guidance's calibration happens to point the same way. If the certificate were the reasoning, then stripping it out would change the answer, and it would not: on this observation the 21:00 bar stands with no certificate at all. The three axes also come apart in the other direction. The UK classification axis is empty [UK-FLM-010], so a reader cannot infer the hour from it even in principle. And the restriction axis is independent of the hour in both directions: clearing 21:00 does not discharge UK-SEX-003, because strong or explicit sexual material still has to be justified by context after the watershed, and UK-CTX-011 is the authority that the content determination and the slot determination are made separately - context defended the material in Toofan and did nothing for the hour. No condition on this record substitutes for the hour. Mandatory daytime protection would be such a substitute [UK-SCH-007], but it is not in place and the slice gives no route to it on a free-to-air service, so 'any time' is not available here and must not be offered.
decisions.reasoning: Routing. is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no', recorded by the extractor from the stated descriptor 'comedy feature', so the news route does not arise and the ordinary Section One analysis applies. Absolute prohibitions first, reading what each covers rather than its label. UK-GEN-001 bars material that might SERIOUSLY impair the development of under-eighteens. That is a deliberately higher bar than ordinary harm, and nothing in o1 approaches it: a comedic sex scene with broad, unrealistic staging and no nudity shown is the ordinary-harm tier, which is schedulable. Treating it as the serious-impairment tier would ban most of what the system exists to schedule. UK-SEX-001 bars material equivalent to the BBFC R18 rating at any time, and this is the prohibition most at risk of being over-applied here, because 'sexual content' is the category key on o1. R18-equivalence turns on explicit material whose character the rule set elsewhere describes by reference to the primary purpose of sexual arousal [UK-SEX-003]. o1 is intercut with reaction shots, scored for laughs, broad and unrealistic, with no nudity shown, and carries a BBFC 15 rather than an 18 or an R18. It is not R18-equivalent, and the rule is not engaged. UK-FLM-001 bars films refused classification by the BBFC: this film holds a BBFC 15, so it was not refused, and the rule is not engaged. UK-FLM-006 bars BBFC R18-rated films: the certificate on file is a 15, so it is not engaged. I note that the scope of the 15 is 'not_stated' - cinema, video or TV is unknown - which affects how much evidential weight the certificate carries, but not whether these prohibitions bite, since none of them turns on a 15. No absolute prohibition bites. Classification, as an independent pass. The UK issues no per-programme age rating for linear television; the Code has in the main dispensed with scheduling by rating [UK-FLM-010] and the statutory instrument is a standards duty rather than a classification scheme [UK-LAW-001]. I emit no_per_programme_rating. Emitting '15' here would be the invented-instrument error, and it would also be the first step towards deriving the hour from the certificate. Hours, as a genuinely independent pass. I start from the observation, not the certificate. o1 records that sexual intercourse is clearly depicted. UK-SEX-004 is directly on point and is the strongest basis in this decision: representations of sexual intercourse must not occur before the watershed unless there is a SERIOUS EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE, and the rule records that this is a higher bar than ordinary editorial justification. A comedy feature scored for laughs plainly does not meet it. So the pre-watershed position is barred, and barred on a conditional rule whose condition is clearly not satisfied rather than on a judgement call. UK-SCH-002 reaches the same 21:00 independently, because clearly depicted intercourse is material unsuitable for children, children meaning under fifteen [UK-DEF-001, UK-SCH-001]. The certificate points the same way through the UK-FLM-010 calibration - it is unlikely a recently BBFC 15-rated film could be scheduled during the day - but that is a presumption drawn from guidance and I have placed it third deliberately, because it is the weakest of the three routes and the one most likely to be mistaken for the reason. Service type is given as free_to_air, so no service branching is required and the 20:00 premium-film displacement is not in issue; no such rule is in the slice in any event. There is no technical-measure route: UK-SCH-007 would remove the hours question entirely while mandatory daytime protection is in place, but no protection is described and the slice contains no rule conferring an any-hour permission on a free-to-air service, so I report with_technical_measure as n/a rather than inventing an unlock. Restrictions, as a third pass, then checked against the hours. Clearing 21:00 does not end the analysis. UK-SEX-003 requires that strong or explicit sexual material which is not adult sex material be justified by the context even after the watershed. The comedic framing, the absence of nudity and the unrealistic staging are the available justification, and on the material described they look capable of supporting it - but that is a provisional view on a judgment_based rule marked human_review_required=yes, and UK-CTX-011 is the authority that the content question and the slot question are decided separately, so a positive answer on context does not purchase the hour. The transition duties [UK-SCH-004, UK-SCH-008] cannot be signed off, and the reason is worth stating plainly: the extractor records that it cannot tell whether the single event listed is the complete event list for the asset or an extract. If it is an extract, nothing is known about the opening minutes, about strong language anywhere in the film, or about any other sexual or violent material - and the 'no other events' reading would be my assumption, not the source's statement. That single uncertainty is what holds this decision's confidence down, because the 21:00 floor is firm but the question of how far above 21:00 is not answerable. The date and slot are not stated, so the gradient within the pre-watershed band [UK-SCH-010] and the festival factor [UK-SCH-011] cannot be applied, and whether a +1 service carries the asset is unknown, so a second transmission decision may be owed [UK-SCH-009]. Finally, nothing in the observations purports to clear the asset, so there is no embedded-instruction problem to report in this case; the BBFC 15 is recorded as a certificate and I have treated it as evidence, not as an answer.
review_reasons: The extractor states it cannot tell whether the single listed event is the complete event list for the asset or an extract covering only that scene, and the source does not say. The 21:00 floor is secure either way, but whether 21:00 itself is adequate - and whether the film opens with strong material, contains strong language, or holds further sexual or violent content - cannot be answered. A person must obtain the full event list or view the asset.

UK-SEX-003 is judgment_based and carries human_review_required=yes: whether the comedic framing, the unrealistic staging and the absence of nudity sufficiently justify strong or explicit sexual material in context is a viewing judgement. My provisional view is that they do, and it should not be relied on.
UK-SCH-004 and UK-SCH-008 (the smooth-transition duty) are judgment_based and marked human_review_required=yes, and cannot be assessed because the opening of the film is not described.

UK-FLM-010 is judgment_based and marked human_review_required=yes. It is also the rule that keeps the certificate in its place, so a reviewer should confirm that the 21:00 answer has not been reached from the '15' by accident - and should note that the certificate's scope (cinema, video or TV) is not stated, which bears on how much indication it supplies.

UK-SCH-010, UK-SCH-011, UK-CTX-010 and UK-WRN-002 and UK-WRN-003 are all judgment_based with human_review_required=yes, and all of them need the date, the slot or the channel - none of which is stated.

intended_slot and intended_date are 'not_stated'. The decision therefore states a floor rather than clearing a proposed transmission, and the proposed transmission must come back for a decision once it exists.
Whether a timeshift or +1 service carries the asset is not stated; if it does, that showing is its own decision [UK-SCH-009], which is conditional and marked human_review_required=yes.

The ages of the characters in o1 are recorded as not stated. On the description the scene is not pornographic, so neither UK-SEX-001 nor the French under-18 prohibition is engaged on its own terms; but a reviewer should confirm the point rather than leave it resting on an inference about a comedy.

missing_information.field: whether the event list is complete, or an extract covering only the 00:48:10 scene
missing_information.why_it_matters: The hours floor rests on o1, but the adequacy of any slot at or near 21:00 depends on what else is in the film and where - in particular the opening minutes, for the smooth-transition duty [UK-SCH-004, UK-SCH-008], and any strong language, which is expressly listed as not stated.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: If the list is complete, 21:00 is likely adequate and confidence rises. If it is an extract, the decision is provisional in substance as well as in form, and a later slot or an edit may be required.

missing_information.field: intended_slot
missing_information.why_it_matters: The decision can state that the asset is barred before 21:00, but cannot clear a transmission that has no proposed time. The pre-watershed band is also a gradient rather than a flat zone [UK-SCH-010].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Turns a floor into a yes or no for a specific showing, and brings the transition duty into play if the start is at or shortly after 21:00.

missing_information.field: intended_date
missing_information.why_it_matters: School holidays and cultural or religious festivals raise the expected child audience without moving the clock [UK-SCH-010, UK-SCH-011], and appropriate scheduling expressly takes school time, weekends and holidays into account [UK-DEF-002].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A 21:00 slot defensible in term time may require a later placement in August or during a festival, with no change to the content.

missing_information.field: the identity of the channel, not merely the delivery type 'free-to-air'
missing_information.why_it_matters: The nature of the channel and the likely audience expectation for that channel at that time and day are express appropriate-scheduling factors [UK-DEF-002], and audience size can make the required justification stricter but never looser [UK-CTX-010].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Determines how much contextual justification the slot demands. 'Free-to-air' is a delivery type and supplies none of this.

missing_information.field: the scope of the BBFC 15 certificate (cinema, video or TV) and how recent it is
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-FLM-010 gives weight to a RECENT BBFC classification as an indication of suitability. An old or differently scoped certificate is weaker evidence.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Changes the evidential weight of the certificate. It does not change the 21:00 floor, which stands on o1 alone - and that independence is the point.

missing_information.field: whether any warning, signposting or on-screen age label accompanies the transmission, and its wording and placement
missing_information.why_it_matters: A warning is one of the main ways a broadcaster earns a slot it would not otherwise get, and it must be adequate in frequency and positioning and must convey severity to count [UK-WRN-002, UK-WRN-003].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: An adequate signpost strengthens a placement close to 21:00. Its absence means no such mitigation may be credited.

missing_information.field: whether a timeshift or +1 service carries the asset, and at what time
missing_information.why_it_matters: Each showing is its own decision and the effective slot moves by an hour [UK-SCH-009].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A 21:00 placement on the main service becomes 22:00 on the +1, which is unproblematic; but a 21:00 placement reached by scheduling the main service at 20:00 would breach, and that is the counter-intuitive direction the rule warns about.

missing_information.field: whether the asset is to be shown in its certificated form or edited for broadcast
missing_information.why_it_matters: Editing changes the material the hours rule is applied to, and the guidance notes that some content remains unsuitable regardless of editing [UK-SCH-006].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: An edit removing or shortening the depiction at 00:48:10 could remove the UK-SEX-004 bar altogether and change the answer to a pre-watershed one.

missing_information.field: the ages of the characters in the 00:48:10 scene
missing_information.why_it_matters: Recorded as not stated. It bears on the prohibitions that turn on under-18s, even though on this description the scene is not pornographic and so those rules are not reached.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Confirms that the under-18 prohibitions are out of scope on the facts, rather than on an inference about the genre.

missing_information.field: whether a trailer or any other derived asset exists, and in what slot
missing_information.why_it_matters: A trailer is assessed in its own slot and does not inherit the feature's permission [UK-TRL-002, UK-TRL-003].
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Adds further transmission decisions, which would very likely be refused for a pre-watershed break if they carried o1.

missing_information.field: what the 'UK, FR' countries field denotes - territory of transmission, production origin, or both
missing_information.why_it_matters: The rules apply to a transmission in the territory. If the field records production origin rather than transmission territory, one or both decisions may be answering the wrong question.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Could remove a country decision from scope entirely.

coverage_gaps: Nothing in the UK slice addresses the one feature of o1 the extractor went out of its way to record: that no nudity is shown. UK-SEX-003 and UK-SEX-004 both turn on the depiction of sexual behaviour and intercourse, and neither distinguishes a depiction without nudity from one with it. The distinction looks as if it ought to matter and the table as given gives it nowhere to land except as an input to the judgment_based context assessment, so it is recorded here rather than silently absorbed.

The comedic treatment is similarly unaccommodated. UK-SEX-004's only pre-watershed escape is a SERIOUS EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE; the slice contains no rule recognising comedy or satire as a relevant treatment for sexual content, although the broader rule set elsewhere treats comedy as carrying real weight. The result is that the comedic framing can affect the post-watershed context judgement [UK-SEX-003] but cannot affect the pre-watershed bar at all. That may well be correct, but it follows from the shape of the table rather than from a rule addressing the point.

The runtime is 'not_stated', and UK-WRN-002 turns on whether a single warning at the beginning suffices 'for a longer programme'. With no runtime there is no way to apply that threshold, so the warning-adequacy question cannot be closed even if a warning were described.

decisions.transmission: t1: free-to-air service, date 'not_stated', start time 'not_stated'. The service type is given, which resolves the French service branch: this is a service 'other than cinema channels and pay-per-view', so the non-cinema-channel limbs of the scheduling rules apply and the cinema-channel and pay-per-view limbs do not. The branch that remains open is the CLASSIFICATION, and in France the hour follows the category, so the hour cannot be fixed. The date is also missing, which independently blocks the FR-SCH-004 derogation.

classification.value: unresolved: most likely III (-12) or IV (-16); cannot be settled from this record. Provisional view, held at low confidence: at least III (-12). Category I (tous publics) is excluded. Category V (-18) is not supported by what is described.
classification.scheme: Arcom / CSA signaletique jeunesse, categories I to V, assigned by the editor's own commission de visionnage

basis.why: Category I is for all audiences with no pictogram. Excluded: a scene in which sexual intercourse is clearly depicted is not programming for all audiences. Cited also for the point that matters most on this axis - it is the EDITOR who classifies, through an internal commission de visionnage. The French category is a determination the broadcaster owes and has not evidenced, so this axis is not merely unknown to me, it is unmade.

Category II (-10) covers programmes certain scenes of which are liable to shock minors under 10. Clearly depicted intercourse would satisfy this, so II is a floor rather than the answer. judgment_based.

Category III (-12) covers works banned to under-12s in cinemas and programmes liable to DISTURB under-12s, in particular where the programme resorts in a repeated way to physical or psychological violence. The violence limb is not engaged - no violence is recorded anywhere in the observations. The 'liable to disturb under-12s' limb does not require violence and is capable of reaching clearly depicted intercourse, which is why III is my provisional floor. The cinema-ban limb cannot apply: the only certificate on file is a BBFC 15, a UK certificate, and there is no French cinema interdiction recorded. The row is judgment_based and marked human_review_required=yes.

The cinema classification MAY serve as an indication for the television classification, but the editor must verify that the rating transfers without harm and may strengthen it - and French practice is explicitly to RAISE the age limit between cinema and television, because a child who could not enter a cinema can easily be in front of a television set. Two cautions follow. First, the BBFC 15 is a UK certificate and this rule speaks of the classification a film receives for cinema release; whether a foreign certificate serves as an indication at all is not addressed by any rule in the slice. Second, even if it does, 15 would be a floor to be raised rather than a ceiling, which cuts against reading the UK answer across to France.

The statutory hook: programmes liable to harm the development of minors must not be made available unless it is ensured, by the choice of broadcast time and/or any appropriate technical process, that minors are not normally liable to see them. Clearly depicted intercourse engages the ordinary-harm tier, which is what puts the asset into the category and hours system at all rather than leaving it unclassified.

hours.permitted: Cannot be stated as a single time, because the category is unresolved and in France the hour follows the category. On this free-to-air service: if the category is II, there is no clock restriction at all, only a placement restriction - it may not be placed within programmes intended for children [FR-SCH-001]. If III, not before 22:00 [FR-SCH-002], subject to the exceptional 20:30 derogation which cannot be assessed without the date [FR-SCH-004]. If IV, not before 22:30 [FR-SCH-005], with no derogation available. My provisional floor is therefore 22:00, and it may be 22:30. What can be said without qualification is that France is later than the UK on this asset whichever of III or IV applies.
hours.without_technical_measure: As above. This is the operative column for France here: the instrument is the hour and the signage, not an access control.
hours.with_technical_measure: n/a. No technical measure is available to this transmission. FR-LAW-002 offers time AND/OR an appropriate technical process as instruments in principle, but the implementing rules for categories II, III and IV state hours and placement and confer no PIN or lock route; the only prescribed locking regime belongs to category V, which is not supported by this record. On a free-to-air service category V is in any event subject to a total prohibition on broadcast [FR-CV-003], so the category V route could not supply an unlock here even if it were reached - it would supply a ban. The UK result must not be read across: no UK finding about access control has any effect on this column.

basis.why: The provisional answer. Category III on services other than cinema channels and pay-per-view must not be broadcast before 22:00. The service is free-to-air, so this is the applicable limb and the cinema-channel limb is not.

If the category is IV (-16), the hour on a non-cinema-channel service is 22:30 and the content is reserved for a warned audience. Included because IV cannot be excluded from this record, and because the row expressly records that no derogation equivalent to FR-SCH-004 exists for category IV - so an answer of 22:30 would be firm in a way that 22:00 is not.

The category III exceptional derogation: after 20:30, except on Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, the eve of public holidays and during school holidays, capped at 16 programmes a year of which at most 4 may be works banned to under-12s in cinemas. Cited because exceptions and allowances move the answer towards permissive and must not be omitted. It cannot be exercised here: it expressly requires the broadcast date and the French school-holiday calendar, both 'not_stated', and the annual quota cannot be verified from a single asset description. Conditional, human_review_required=yes.

If the category settles at II, the hours axis is empty - timing is left to the editor's discretion - and the real restriction is a placement rule. Reported so that a clock-only reading does not record 'no restriction' where a placement restriction exists.

Recorded to show the category V route was tested and not taken: category V broadcast is governed entirely by Recommandation 2004-7. Nothing in o1 engages category V - a comedic scene with no nudity shown is not the pornographic or very-violent material that regime addresses - so its window is not reached.

The consequence if that view were wrong, stated so it is visible rather than buried: on a service not eligible under the cinema-channel and pay-per-view gate, category V is subject to a TOTAL PROHIBITION on broadcast. This transmission is free-to-air, so a category V finding here would mean no permitted time at all, not a late slot. bright_line, human_review_required=yes.

The hours exist to ensure that minors are not normally liable to see or hear material liable to harm their development, by the choice of broadcast time and/or an appropriate technical process. It governs the hours axis and confirms the instruments are alternatives in principle even where the implementing rules offer only the hour.

other_restrictions.requirement: From category II upwards: the pictogram must remain on screen FOR THE WHOLE DURATION of the programme; a written mention must appear either at the bottom of the screen in white for at least one minute at the start or full-screen for at least twelve seconds before the programme, with the wording set by category ('deconseille aux moins de douze ans' for III, 'aux moins de seize ans' for IV); and the classification must be made known to the public at the time of broadcast, in trailers, and in programme schedules communicated to the press. These stack on top of whatever hour applies - none of them substitutes for it. This is the clearest divergence from the UK, which imposes no on-screen pictogram and discharges the equivalent function through information.

At category II the governing restriction is placement rather than time: the programme may not be placed within programmes intended for children. At category III, trailers may not air close to children's programmes. Either way a placement check is owed that no clock test performs, and the observations give no information about surrounding programming.

Conditional and not triggered on the facts given: no trailer is described. If one exists it must carry the pictogram of the programme's category THROUGHOUT and must not contain scenes likely to offend young viewers - which o1 would be - and if the category settles at IV, a category IV trailer may not air before 20:30. Recorded so that a derived asset is not cleared by silence.

If the category settles at IV, the content is 'reserved for a warned audience' as a term of the permission itself, not as an optional mitigation. That is a condition of the 22:30 hour rather than an extra on top of it.

If the category settles at III, the FR-SCH-004 derogation is a real allowance that must be put to a person rather than ignored: it would permit a 20:30 start on a permitted weekday outside school holidays, within an annual cap of 16 programmes and a sub-cap of 4 works banned to under-12s in cinemas. It cannot be exercised from this record and it does not exist for category IV, so it must not be generalised.

Recorded as considered and not engaged, and as the one route by which this asset could be barred outright in France: category V is totally prohibited on services that are not cinema channels or pay-per-view, and this transmission is free-to-air. Nothing in the observations supports category V, so the prohibition is not applied - but a reviewer reclassifying upwards to V would be refusing the transmission, not moving it later.

Recorded as unavailable rather than unconsidered: the reclassification procedure allows works at least twenty years past their last visa to be submitted for revision for television broadcast, by joint request of editor and producer at least eight months before scheduling. It cannot be used here - there is no French visa on file at all, only a BBFC 15, and its date is unknown - but it is the only route by which the classification commission revisits a rating for television, so a reviewer should know it exists and that this asset does not obviously qualify for it.

decisions.axis_note: France is the mirror image of the UK on this asset, and the contrast is the useful output. The UK has no classification to give and a firm hour; France has a classification that drives everything and that nobody has yet made, so the hour is unresolved. Within France the hour is derived from the category and not from the content directly, which is exactly the derivation the UK forbids - so the two countries cannot share a reasoning path even though they are looking at one scene. The category also does not predict the restrictions straightforwardly: at II the hours axis is empty and the restriction is a placement rule [FR-SCH-001], so a clock-only reading would report 'no restriction' for the category whose real constraint is about what the programme sits inside. No condition here substitutes for an hour. The signage duties [FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002, FR-SIG-003] are cumulative with whatever hour applies, and the one French regime with a technical measure is category V, which on a free-to-air service is not an unlock at all but a total prohibition [FR-CV-003]. The 'warned audience' term of category IV [FR-SCH-005] is the only condition on this record that is genuinely part of the hour rather than additional to it. Finally, the UK finding that the comedic framing contextualises the material has no counterpart here: France's category test asks whether scenes are liable to shock or disturb minors of a given age, which is not the same question, and no rule in this slice makes treatment a defence.
decisions.reasoning: Absolute prohibitions first, reading what each covers rather than its category label - and this case is where that instruction does the most work, because the single observation carries the content_category 'sexual_content' and two of the French prohibitions sit under sexual or dignity headings. FR-PRO-002 bans PORNOGRAPHIC programmes DEPICTING UNDER-18s. It carries the sexual_content category key, and the prompt is explicit that applying it on the strength of that label would refuse an ordinary title. It is not engaged, and it fails on the first limb before the second is reached: o1 describes a scene with broad, unrealistic staging, scored for laughs, intercut with reaction shots, with no nudity shown, carrying a BBFC 15. That is not pornography. I note separately that the ages of the characters are recorded as not stated, so the second limb cannot be confirmed from the record either; I have not resolved it by assumption, and I have not needed to, because the first limb is not met. FR-PRO-001 bans programmes which offend human dignity, in particular those depicting sexual violence, perversions or degradation. Nothing in o1 describes violence, coercion, or degradation of any participant, and the general dignity head does not reach a consensual comedic depiction. Not engaged. FR-PRO-003 bans programmes of extreme or gratuitous violence: there is no violence anywhere in the observations. Not engaged. FR-LAW-001 bans programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm - nuire gravement - the development of minors, which is tier 1 of the two-tier French standard and a deliberately higher bar than the ordinary harm of FR-LAW-002. Clearly depicted intercourse in a comedy engages tier 2, not tier 1; treating the two as one tier would ban most of what is schedulable. So no absolute prohibition bites, and the asset goes into the category and hours system. Classification, as an independent pass, and this is where the French decision stops short. The editor classifies, through its own commission de visionnage [FR-CLS-001], and no such determination is in evidence. Category I is excluded by o1. Category II is satisfied and so is a floor rather than an answer [FR-CLS-002]. Category III is my provisional floor: its violence limb is not engaged, because no violence is recorded, but its other limb - programmes liable to DISTURB under-12s - does not require violence and is readily capable of reaching clearly depicted intercourse [FR-CLS-003]. Whether the material instead reaches category IV (-16) I cannot say, and here I have to be plain about a gap in the rules I was given: the slice contains the category IV HOURS [FR-SCH-005] and the category IV trailer rule [FR-TRL-003], but no row stating the category IV THRESHOLD. So I have the consequence of a category IV finding without the test for making one, and I decline to invent the test. That is recorded as a coverage gap and it is the main reason the French classification is reported as unresolved between III and IV rather than settled at III. The BBFC 15 helps less than it appears to. FR-FLM-001 says a cinema classification may serve as an indication but the editor must verify it transfers without harm and may strengthen it, and French practice is explicitly to RAISE the age limit for television. Two problems follow: the certificate is a UK one and no rule in the slice says whether a foreign certificate serves as an indication at all; and if it does, 15 is a floor to be raised rather than a ceiling, which points towards IV rather than away from it. Reading the UK's 21:00 across to France would be wrong twice over - wrong in method, because France derives the hour from a category, and wrong in direction, because French practice raises rather than preserves the age. Hours, as an independent pass. Service type is given as free_to_air, which resolves the French service branch cleanly: this is a service other than a cinema channel or pay-per-view, so the 22:00 limb for category III applies [FR-SCH-002] and the Wednesday-20:30 cinema-channel limb does not. If the category is IV the hour is 22:30 and no derogation exists [FR-SCH-005]; if II, there is no clock restriction at all and only a placement rule [FR-SCH-001]. I have applied the FR-SCH-004 derogation as an allowance to be put to a reviewer rather than omitting it, because a system modelling only prohibitions over-restricts - but it cannot be exercised here, since it turns on the weekday, public-holiday eves, the school-holiday calendar and an annual quota, and intended_date is not stated. There is no technical-measure column to fill: the only French locking regime is category V's, and on this free-to-air service a category V finding would produce a total prohibition rather than an unlock [FR-CV-003]. I have stated that explicitly, because reporting a bar without an available measure and reporting a measure that does not exist are both errors, and the honest position is that France offers no measure here. Restrictions, as a third pass, checked against the hours. The signage duties attach from category II upwards and are cumulative with the hour [FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002, FR-SIG-003]; note that the pictogram must be on screen for the whole duration, which is an obligation with no UK analogue and which a UK-trained pipeline will miss entirely. The placement restriction at category II [FR-SCH-001] and the trailer-adjacency rule at category III [FR-TRL-002] are restrictions a clock-based reading cannot see. Category IV's 'warned audience' [FR-SCH-005] is a condition of the hour rather than an addition to it, and I have marked it as such. Finally, the runtime is not stated, which matters more in France than in the UK: FR-SIG-001 requires the pictogram for the whole duration of the broadcast, so the obligation is well defined whatever the runtime, but the editor cannot discharge FR-SIG-002's one-minute written mention or plan the signage without knowing the programme's shape.
review_reasons: The classification is unresolved between III (-12) and IV (-16), and in France the hour follows the category. FR-CLS-002 and FR-CLS-003 are both judgment_based and FR-CLS-003 carries human_review_required=yes. The determination belongs to the editor's own commission de visionnage [FR-CLS-001] and has not been made.

The slice supplies the category IV hours [FR-SCH-005] and the category IV trailer rule [FR-TRL-003] but no row stating the category IV threshold. I therefore cannot test for the category whose hour would be 22:30, and I have not invented the test. A French reviewer with the full instrument must settle this.

No rule in the slice addresses depicted sexual content as a classification input. The French category rules in front of me speak of shocking under-10s, disturbing under-12s and repeated violence; the UK has a rule directly on intercourse [UK-SEX-004] and France, as given, does not. The French category is therefore being inferred from a general 'liable to disturb' test rather than applied.

intended_date is 'not_stated', so the FR-SCH-004 derogation cannot be assessed: it turns on the weekday, public-holiday eves, the French school-holiday calendar and an annual quota invisible from a single asset description. The row is conditional and marked human_review_required=yes.
intended_slot is 'not_stated', so there is no proposed time to test against 22:00 or 22:30.

The extractor cannot tell whether the single listed event is the complete event list or an extract. A French category must be assigned to the whole work, so an incomplete event list is a more serious obstacle here than in the UK, where a floor could still be stated.

FR-CV-003 is bright_line and marked human_review_required=yes. It is in the decision as the route by which an upward reclassification to V would refuse this free-to-air transmission outright rather than move it later, and a reviewer should see that consequence explicitly.

Whether a foreign (BBFC) certificate serves as an indication under FR-FLM-001 at all is not addressed by any rule in the slice, and FR-FLM-001 is itself judgment_based. The temptation to carry the UK '15' into the French category must be resisted, and French practice is to raise rather than preserve the age.

basis.why: A BBFC certificate does not set the slot: the Ofcom Code has in the main dispensed with the legacy rules relating scheduling to ratings, and films are scheduled like any other content, appropriately for the audience. So '15' is not the UK output. The certificate does carry evidential weight, and the guidance supplies a calibration from it which matters here: since children means under fifteen and material unsuitable for children should not generally be shown before 21:00, it is UNLIKELY that a RECENTLY BBFC 15-rated film could be scheduled during the day. That is a presumption against daytime, not a prohibition, and it is the only thing on this record pointing towards a restriction that the observations themselves do not supply.

The statutory duty is to set standards securing that under-eighteens are protected. The instrument produced is a standards code applied at the point of scheduling, not a per-programme classification scheme, so the UK classification axis is empty by design rather than unresolved.

hours.permitted: Not fully resolved, and the honest shape of the answer is asymmetric. ESTABLISHED: a post-21:00 transmission is permissible on the material recorded, subject to the context duties below [UK-SCH-002, UK-SEX-003, UK-OFF-001]. NOT ESTABLISHED, in either direction: whether a pre-21:00 slot is available. No rule in this slice imposes an outright pre-watershed bar on what is recorded - and that is the finding most at risk of being got wrong in the restrictive direction. But three things stop a pre-watershed slot being cleared: the 'sustained' explicit sexual dialogue at o1 must be editorially justified AND APPROPRIATELY LIMITED to run before the watershed [UK-SEX-004], and 'sustained' sits in tension with 'appropriately limited'; the certificate creates a presumption against DAYTIME placement [UK-FLM-010]; and the event list is not stated to be complete, with the actual words used at o1 expressly unknown. So: no daytime slot on this record; a later pre-watershed evening slot is arguable but unproven; 21:00 and after is clear.

basis.why: The rule that decides the shape of this case, and it must be read in two halves. Its first limb - representations of sexual intercourse must not occur before the watershed absent a serious educational purpose - is NOT engaged: o1 is dialogue, is_depicted is false, and the source says expressly that no sexual activity is shown. Applying the first limb here would be the over-restriction error, and it would produce a 21:00 bar that the rule does not impose. Its second limb IS engaged: any DISCUSSION OR PORTRAYAL of sexual behaviour before the watershed must be editorially justified and appropriately limited. That is a standard, not a bar. The comedic framing supplies editorial justification; whether dialogue the source itself calls 'sustained' is 'appropriately limited' is the open question, and it is the reason a pre-watershed slot cannot simply be cleared.

o2. Nudity before the watershed must be justified by the context - and the rule records expressly that nudity is NOT automatically post-watershed and that context can justify it earlier. A man's bare chest in a comedic waxing scene is about as easily context-justified as nudity gets, and the extractor itself notes that a reviewer may consider a bare chest outside the intended sense of the category. So this observation does not drive the hour. Recording it as a 21:00 trigger because the category label reads 'nudity' would be a clear over-restriction. judgment_based and marked human_review_required=yes, so the view is provisional.

The general watershed: material unsuitable for children should not in general be shown before 21:00 or after 05:30. Cited for the established half of the answer - a post-21:00 placement raises no watershed question - and because it is the rule against which any proposed pre-watershed slot would be tested once the open facts are supplied.

The operative duty: children must be protected by appropriate scheduling from material unsuitable for them. Applied to o1, o2 and o3, the question is whether sustained explicit sexual dialogue is unsuitable for people under fifteen. On the recorded material - nothing shown, comic framing - this is a genuine judgement rather than an obvious yes, which is why the pre-watershed position is reported as open rather than barred.

'Children' in the operative scheduling rules means people under fifteen. The certificate is also a 15, and the coincidence must not be read as causation - UK-FLM-010 is explicit that the certificate does not set the slot.

Appropriate scheduling is judged on the nature of the content, the likely number and age range of child viewers taking into account school time, weekends and holidays, the start and finish time, the nature of the channel, and audience expectation. The start time, the date and the channel are all unknown, which is why a specific pre-watershed slot cannot be assessed.

Cited on the hours axis as well, and deliberately: the certificate's calibration - it is unlikely that a recently BBFC 15-rated film could be scheduled during the day - is a presumption against daytime that the observations alone would not generate. It is weak authority (rank 3, judgment_based, guidance rather than Code text) and it is a presumption rather than a rule, so it bounds the answer without supplying it. Note too that the certificate's scope and date are both unstated, and the calibration speaks of a RECENT classification, so even that presumption cannot be applied at full strength.

If a pre-watershed slot is proposed, where in the band it sits matters: the expectation is strongest approaching 19:30 and during school holidays, so the band is a gradient rather than a flat zone. With no slot and no date this cannot be applied, and it cannot be applied in the broadcaster's favour either.
A cultural or religious festival raises the expected child audience without moving the clock. intended_date is not stated, so this check has not been run.

Whether a timeshift service carries the asset is not stated. If it does, the effective slot moves by an hour in either direction, and the counter-intuitive direction matters here: a pre-watershed placement chosen because children are at school lands an hour later, when they are home.

Considered and not engaged. The watershed would not apply at all while mandatory daytime protection is in place, but no protection is described on this free-to-air transmission. Recorded so the reviewer can see the substitution route was tested.

other_restrictions.requirement: After the watershed, strong or explicit sexual language that is not 'adult sex material' must still be justified by the context. o1 is explicit sexual language, so this duty is live even for a 21:00 or later placement. The comedic framing, the fact that nothing is shown, and the film's evident purpose are the available justification and look capable of supporting it; that is a provisional view on a judgment_based rule marked human_review_required=yes. Clearing the hour does not discharge this, and context justifying the material does not by itself justify the slot - the two are decided separately.

decisions.axis_note: This case is the over-restriction trap, and the three axes come apart in the permissive direction rather than the restrictive one. The classification axis is empty: no per-programme rating is issued for UK linear television [UK-FLM-010]. The hours axis is NOT given by the certificate, and here that cuts in the broadcaster's favour: a category-driven read sees 'sexual_content' and 'nudity' on a BBFC 15 film and produces 21:00, but the rules do not. UK-SEX-004's hard pre-watershed bar is about REPRESENTATIONS of sexual intercourse and nothing is represented - o1 is dialogue with is_depicted false - so what applies is its softer second limb, a justified-and-appropriately-limited standard. UK-NUD-001 expressly states that nudity is not automatically post-watershed and that context can justify it earlier, so a bare male chest in a comedy does not supply an hour either. The only thing on this record pushing against a daytime placement is the certificate's calibration in UK-FLM-010, which is a presumption and rank 3 guidance, not a rule. So the restriction axis is doing most of the work: the live obligations are the context duties on explicit sexual language [UK-SEX-003] and on pain played for comedy [UK-OFF-001], and these do not reduce to an hour - they survive a post-watershed placement and must be satisfied separately. UK-CTX-011 is the authority for exactly that separation: context defended the material in Toofan and did nothing for the slot. No condition on this record substitutes for an hour, because the one substitution mechanism - mandatory daytime protection disapplying the watershed [UK-SCH-007] - is not available on a free-to-air service with no protection described. It is worth saying plainly what the honest output is: the rating does not predict the hours, and in this case it over-predicts them.
decisions.reasoning: Routing. is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no', recorded from the stated descriptor 'comedy feature', so the ordinary Section One analysis applies. Absolute prohibitions first, reading what each covers rather than its label - and here they are the error to avoid, not the answer. UK-GEN-001 bars material that might SERIOUSLY impair the development of under-eighteens, a deliberately higher bar than ordinary harm. Nothing in these observations approaches it: explicit sexual dialogue with nothing shown, a bare male chest, and comic pain. UK-SEX-001 bars material equivalent to the BBFC R18 rating at any time, and it is the prohibition most likely to be mis-fired here because o1 carries the content_category 'sexual_content'. R18-equivalence turns on explicit material whose character is set by reference to the primary purpose of sexual arousal; o1 is comic dialogue in which nothing is depicted, on a film certificated 15. Not engaged, and not close. UK-FLM-001 bars films refused classification by the BBFC: this film holds a BBFC 15, so it was not refused. UK-FLM-006 bars BBFC R18-rated films: the certificate is a 15. Neither is engaged, and I decline to infer a different certificate from the fact that the scope of this one is unstated. No absolute prohibition bites. Classification, as an independent pass. The UK issues no per-programme age rating for linear television [UK-FLM-010, UK-LAW-001], so I emit no_per_programme_rating. Emitting '15' would be an invented instrument and would also be the first step towards deriving the hour from the certificate. Hours, as a genuinely independent pass, starting from the observations. This is where the case turns, and it turns on a careful reading of UK-SEX-004 rather than on its headline. Its first sentence bars REPRESENTATIONS of sexual intercourse before the watershed unless there is a serious educational purpose. o1 is not a representation: is_depicted is false, treatment is 'reported_not_shown', and the source states explicitly that no sexual activity is shown. So the hard bar is not engaged. That is the single most important finding in this decision, because the superficially similar case - a comedy with the same certificate on the same service where intercourse IS clearly depicted - would be barred before 21:00 by this very rule, and the difference between the two is whether anything is shown, not what the certificate says. The rule's second sentence does apply: any discussion or portrayal of sexual behaviour before the watershed must be editorially justified and appropriately limited. The comedic framing is editorial justification. Whether dialogue the source itself calls 'sustained' is 'appropriately limited' I cannot determine, because the duration is unstated and the actual words are unstated, and the second limb is the kind of standard whose answer depends on exactly those facts. o2 does not supply an hour. UK-NUD-001 requires nudity before the watershed to be justified by the context, and records in terms that nudity is not automatically post-watershed and that context can justify it earlier. A man's bare chest during a comedic chest-waxing scene is readily justified, and the extractor itself flags that it used 'nudity' as the nearest controlled-vocabulary value for an uncovered body and that a reviewer may consider a bare chest outside the category's intended sense. Treating this as a watershed trigger would be an over-restriction driven by a category key. I also considered and rejected the pre-watershed music-video rule about performers inadequately covered: its scope is music videos and this asset is a film, so it does not apply, though its calibration - what matters is whether the clothing is presented sexually - supports the same conclusion by analogy. o3 is not an hours question at all: comic pain is an offence-and-context matter [UK-OFF-001], not a scheduling one, and nothing in the slice makes it watershed-bound. So the observations do not produce a pre-watershed bar. What stops me clearing a daytime slot is three things, and I want to be explicit that none of them is the certificate standing alone. First, the UK-SEX-004 second limb, unresolved for want of the duration and the words. Second, the UK-FLM-010 calibration, which supplies a presumption that a recently BBFC 15-rated film is unlikely to be schedulable during the day - weak authority, rank 3, judgment_based, and weakened further because the certificate's scope and date are both unstated while the calibration speaks of a recent classification. Third, and most consequentially, the event list cannot be relied on as complete: the not_stated list records that whether any sexual activity, nudity or strong language occurs ANYWHERE ELSE in the asset is unknown, and that only two source events are listed. Strong language is the specific worry, and it has an additional dimension I must flag: the extractor deliberately did not record a strong_language observation, because the source says the acts are described 'in explicit terms' without quoting a word or saying expletives are used. So I do not know whether o1 is explicit anatomically or explicit profanely, and those are different compliance questions. Worse, the rule slice I was given contains NO language rule of any kind, so even if the answer were supplied I would have nothing to apply to it. That is recorded as a coverage gap, and it is a real limit on this decision rather than a formality. The result is an asymmetric answer, which I think is the correct one: post-21:00 is permissible on what is recorded; no daytime slot can be cleared; a later pre-watershed evening slot is arguable and unproven. Restrictions, as a third pass, then checked against the hours. UK-SEX-003 keeps the explicit sexual language live even post-watershed - clearing 21:00 does not discharge it - and UK-OFF-001 keeps o3 live at any hour. Neither is cured by the clock, and UK-CTX-011 is the authority that the content determination and the slot determination are separate, so a favourable context finding on either does not purchase an earlier hour. The transition duties cannot be signed off because the opening is unknown. No warning is described, so none may be credited, which matters because a signposted placement is one of the few routes to an earlier slot. Finally, nothing in the observations purports to clear the asset or instruct an outcome, so there is no embedded-instruction problem in this case; the BBFC 15 is treated as evidence feeding UK-FLM-010, not as an answer.
review_reasons: The pre-watershed question is genuinely open and finely balanced, and it is the question the broadcaster will actually want answered. UK-SEX-004's hard bar is not engaged because nothing is shown, so no rule in the slice bars a pre-watershed transmission outright; but its second limb requires the sexual discussion to be 'appropriately limited', and the source calls the dialogue 'sustained' without giving its duration. A person must decide whether sustained explicit sexual dialogue is appropriately limited for a pre-watershed audience.

The actual words used at 00:09:30 are expressly unknown, and the extractor deliberately did not record a strong_language observation because the source does not quote any word or say expletives are used. Whether o1 is anatomically explicit or profanely explicit is a different compliance question - and the rule slice contains no language rule at all, so the system cannot answer it even if told.

The event list cannot be relied on as complete: the not_stated list records that whether any sexual activity, nudity or strong language occurs anywhere else in the asset is unknown, and only two source events are listed. A pre-watershed clearance on an incomplete list would be unsafe.

UK-NUD-001 is judgment_based and carries human_review_required=yes. My provisional view is that a bare male chest in a comedic waxing scene is easily context-justified and does not drive the hour, and a reviewer should confirm that the permissive reading is right - the extractor itself flags that it used 'nudity' as the nearest available category and that a bare chest may fall outside its intended sense.
UK-SEX-003 is judgment_based with human_review_required=yes: whether explicit sexual language is justified by the context is a viewing judgement that survives the hour.

o3 fits no content category cleanly. The extractor used 'offence_general' and flagged it; I have routed it to UK-OFF-001, which is judgment_based. A reviewer should confirm both the routing and the conclusion that comic pain is contextually justified.

UK-FLM-010 is judgment_based with human_review_required=yes, and it is the only authority on this record pointing against a daytime slot. A reviewer should weigh how much a presumption drawn from guidance should carry, especially given that the certificate's scope and date are unstated while the calibration speaks of a RECENT classification.

UK-SCH-004 and UK-SCH-008 (smooth transition), UK-SCH-010, UK-SCH-011, UK-CTX-010, UK-CTX-011, UK-WRN-002, UK-WRN-003 and UK-TRL-003 are all judgment_based or conditional with human_review_required=yes, and each needs the slot, the date, the channel or the opening of the film - none of which is stated.
intended_slot and intended_date are 'not_stated', so no specific transmission is being cleared. Whether a +1 service carries the asset is also unknown [UK-SCH-009].

classification.scheme: Arcom / CSA signaletique jeunesse, categories I to V, assigned by the editor's own commission de visionnage

basis.why: Category II (-10) covers programmes CERTAIN SCENES of which are liable to shock minors under 10. o1 - sustained dialogue describing sexual acts in explicit terms - is the obvious candidate, and 'certain scenes' fits a single sustained sequence precisely. This is my provisional answer. judgment_based.

Category I is for all audiences and carries no pictogram. It cannot be dismissed outright: nothing is depicted anywhere in the observations, o2 is a bare male chest and o3 is comic pain, and a film whose strongest recorded element is explicit sexual TALK might be classified I by an editor's commission. I think II is more likely, because explicit description of sexual acts is capable of shocking a child under ten even unillustrated. But the distinction between I and II is exactly the judgement the commission exists to make, and it is the editor who classifies - so this axis is unmade rather than merely unknown to me, and the difference between I and II is the difference between no obligations at all and a full signage regime.

Category III (-12) covers works banned to under-12s in cinemas and programmes liable to DISTURB under-12s, in particular where the programme resorts in a REPEATED way to physical or psychological violence. Not supported: there is no violence of any kind in the observations, so the repetition limb is not engaged, and the cinema-ban limb cannot apply because the only certificate on file is a BBFC 15, a UK certificate, with no French interdiction recorded. The 'liable to disturb under-12s' limb does not require violence, so III cannot be formally excluded, but nothing in what is described reaches it. The row is judgment_based and marked human_review_required=yes.

The cinema classification may serve as an INDICATION for the television classification, but the editor must verify that the rating transfers without harm and may STRENGTHEN it, and French practice is explicitly to RAISE the age limit between cinema and television. Two cautions. The certificate here is a BBFC 15, a UK certificate, and this rule speaks of the classification a film receives for cinema release without addressing foreign ones - so its route into the French decision is undefined. And if it were used, it would be a floor to be raised rather than a ceiling, which would point towards a HIGHER French category than the content alone suggests. That pull must be resisted on this record, because the observations do not support it: a 15 certificate paired with three mild recorded events is a reason to ask what is missing from the event list, not a reason to classify upwards on faith.

The statutory hook: programmes liable to HARM the development of minors must not be made available unless it is ensured, by the choice of broadcast time and/or any appropriate technical process, that minors are not normally liable to see them. Whether sustained explicit sexual dialogue is liable to harm the development of minors at all is the threshold question, and if it is not, the asset sits at category I with no restriction. judgment_based.

hours.permitted: Depends on the category, and on the provisional category the answer is permissive. If the category is I: NO time restriction at all [FR-CLS-001]. If II, which is my provisional view: NO clock restriction either - timing is left to the editor's discretion - but the programme MAY NOT BE PLACED WITHIN PROGRAMMES INTENDED FOR CHILDREN [FR-SCH-001]. So the French restriction on this asset is a placement rule rather than an hour, and a system that reported only a clock would record 'unrestricted' and miss the only constraint there is. If the category were III, the hour would be 22:00 on this free-to-air service [FR-SCH-002], subject to the FR-SCH-004 derogation; that branch is listed because III cannot be formally excluded, not because the record supports it.
hours.without_technical_measure: As above. The French instrument here is placement and signage, not an hour and not an access control.
hours.with_technical_measure: n/a. No technical measure is available or needed. FR-LAW-002 offers time and/or an appropriate technical process as instruments in principle, but the implementing rules at categories I to III confer no PIN or lock route; the only prescribed locking regime belongs to category V, which is nowhere near this material, and on a free-to-air service a category V finding would be a total prohibition rather than an unlock [FR-CV-003].

basis.why: The operative rule on the provisional category. At category II the broadcast timing is left to the editor's discretion and there is NO clock restriction; what the rule imposes instead is that such programmes may not be placed within programmes intended for children, with particular care for trailers scheduled near children's programmes. Conditional, and the condition is about surrounding programming rather than about the clock - which is why the placement information the observations do not supply matters more here than any time.

If the category is I there is no restriction of any kind and no pictogram. Reported so the most permissive branch is visible rather than silently dropped - a system modelling only prohibitions would over-restrict, and on this record category I is a live possibility.

The hour if the category were III on this free-to-air service: not before 22:00. Listed as the branch that would apply if a reviewer classified higher than I expect, so the consequence of that reclassification is visible. The service is free-to-air, so this limb and not the cinema-channel limb would be the one to apply.

If the category were III, the exceptional derogation would permit broadcast after 20:30 except on Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, the eve of public holidays and during school holidays, capped at 16 programmes a year. Cited because allowances must not be omitted, and recorded as unusable on this record: it expressly requires the broadcast date and the French school-holiday calendar, both 'not_stated', and the annual quota cannot be verified from a single asset description. Conditional, human_review_required=yes.

Recorded as considered and not reached: category IV (-16) on a non-cinema-channel service would be 22:30 and reserved for a warned audience, with no derogation available. Nothing in the observations supports IV. I note separately that the slice gives me the category IV HOURS but no row stating the category IV THRESHOLD, so even if a reviewer wanted to test for IV, the test is not in the table.
Recorded to show the category V route was tested and not taken: category V broadcast is governed entirely by Recommandation 2004-7. Nothing here engages it.

The consequence if that view were somehow wrong, stated so it is visible: on a service not eligible as a cinema channel or pay-per-view, category V is subject to a TOTAL PROHIBITION on broadcast. This transmission is free-to-air, so a category V finding would mean no permitted time at all rather than a late slot. bright_line, human_review_required=yes.

The hours exist to ensure minors are not normally liable to see or hear material liable to harm their development. On this record the harm question is itself open, which is why the hours axis may be genuinely empty rather than merely permissive.

other_restrictions.requirement: THE OPERATIVE FRENCH RESTRICTION on the provisional category, and it is not an hour: a category II programme may not be placed WITHIN programmes intended for children, and particular care is required for trailers scheduled near children's programmes. The observations say nothing at all about surrounding programming, so this obligation can be stated but not verified, and it cannot be signed off. If the category is I, it falls away entirely.

If the category is II or above: the pictogram must remain on screen FOR THE WHOLE DURATION of the programme; a written mention must appear either at the bottom of the screen in white for at least one minute at the start or full-screen for at least twelve seconds before the programme, worded 'deconseille aux moins de dix ans' for category II; and the classification must be made known to the public at the time of broadcast, in trailers, and in programme schedules communicated to the press. These are cumulative obligations and none substitutes for anything. They are also the whole of the French burden on this asset if the category is II, since there is no hour - so the signage IS the compliance measure here, which is the opposite of how a watershed-shaped model would represent it. If the category is I, none of them applies and there is no pictogram at all.

Conditional and not triggered on the facts given: no trailer is described. If one exists and the category is II or above, it must carry the pictogram of the programme's category THROUGHOUT and must not contain scenes likely to offend young viewers. Note that the trailer content test is independent of the feature's category: a trailer built from the o1 dialogue would raise the 'scenes likely to offend young viewers' question whatever the feature's classification turns out to be.

Recorded as unavailable rather than unconsidered: the reclassification procedure allows works at least twenty years past their last visa to be submitted for revision for television, by joint request of editor and producer at least eight months before scheduling. It cannot be used here - there is no French visa on file at all, only a BBFC 15, whose date is unknown - but it is the only route by which the classification commission revisits a rating for television purposes, and a reviewer should see that it was considered.

Recorded as considered and not engaged, and included because it is the one route by which this asset could be barred outright in France: category V is totally prohibited on services that are not cinema channels or pay-per-view, and this transmission is free-to-air. Nothing in the observations comes close to category V, so the prohibition is not applied - but a reviewer should see that an upward reclassification to V would refuse the transmission rather than move it later.

decisions.axis_note: France inverts the usual expectation on this asset, and the inversion is the main output. The classification axis carries everything - it is the editor's determination through its own commission de visionnage [FR-CLS-001] and it has not been made - while the HOURS axis is probably empty. At category II there is no clock restriction at all; the rule leaves timing to the editor's discretion and imposes a PLACEMENT restriction instead [FR-SCH-001]. At category I there is nothing. So the French answer is most likely 'any hour, with signage, and not inside children's programming', and a pipeline that models France as a set of watershed times would report either a wrong restriction or a wrong clearance: wrong restriction if it reaches for 22:00 by analogy with the UK, wrong clearance if it finds no clock rule and concludes there is no obligation. The restrictions axis is therefore where the entire French burden sits, and it is substantial: the pictogram must be on screen for the WHOLE DURATION of the programme [FR-SIG-001], with a written mention and press-schedule disclosure [FR-SIG-002, FR-SIG-003]. Those obligations have no UK counterpart in any form. No condition here substitutes for an hour, because there is no hour to substitute for; the signage and the placement rule are simply what compliance consists of. And the category does not predict them smoothly: the step from I to II is the step from no obligation at all to the full signage regime, with no change in the hour either way.
decisions.reasoning: Absolute prohibitions first, reading what each covers rather than its label - and on this record all four are rejected, which is itself the point, because three of the four sit under headings that the observation categories would key into. FR-PRO-002 bans PORNOGRAPHIC programmes DEPICTING UNDER-18s. It carries the content_category 'sexual_content', which is also the category on o1, and the prompt is explicit that applying it on the strength of that label would refuse an ordinary title. It fails on both limbs: o1 is comic dialogue in which nothing is depicted at all - is_depicted is false and the source says no sexual activity is shown - so there is no pornography and nothing depicted of anyone. I note that the ages of the characters are recorded as not stated; I have not resolved that by assumption and have not needed to, because the first limb fails. FR-PRO-001 bans programmes which offend human dignity, in particular those depicting sexual violence, perversions or degradation. The nearest candidate is o3, a man having his chest waxed and shouting in pain, played for comedy - pain inflicted on a person for an audience's amusement is the kind of fact that can raise a dignity question. It does not raise it here: the scene is consensual grooming played as farce, there is no coercion, no sexual element and nothing describable as degradation, and the general dignity head does not reach it. FR-PRO-003 bans programmes of extreme or gratuitous violence: there is no violence anywhere in the observations, and comic pain in a waxing scene is not violence - no assault, weapon or attack is described, which the extractor also records. FR-LAW-001 bans programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm - nuire gravement - the development of minors, tier 1 of the two-tier French standard and a deliberately higher bar than the ordinary harm of FR-LAW-002. Nothing here is in that tier; on this record it is doubtful whether even tier 2 is engaged. No prohibition bites. Classification, as an independent pass, and this is the whole French decision. The editor classifies through its own commission de visionnage [FR-CLS-001] and no determination is in evidence. My provisional view is category II (-10): o1 is a scene liable to shock a minor under ten, because explicit description of sexual acts can shock a child even with nothing shown, and 'certain scenes' in FR-CLS-002 fits a single sustained sequence exactly. But category I is genuinely live, and I want to say so rather than default upwards: nothing is depicted anywhere in the asset as described, o2 is a bare male chest and o3 is slapstick. An editor's commission could reasonably classify this I. I have reported the axis as unresolved between I and II for that reason, and because the step between them is consequential - I carries no pictogram and no obligations, II carries the full signage regime. Category III is not supported: its violence limb is not engaged because there is no violence, and its cinema-ban limb cannot apply because the only certificate is a UK one. The BBFC 15 deserves care here, because it pulls in the restrictive direction and should not be allowed to. FR-FLM-001 makes a cinema classification an indication only, requires the editor to verify that it transfers, and records that French practice is to RAISE the age between cinema and television. Read carelessly, that would turn a UK 15 into a French -16 or worse. Two things stop it. First, the rule speaks of the classification a film receives for cinema release and nothing in the slice addresses whether a FOREIGN certificate serves as an indication at all, so its route into this decision is undefined. Second, and more importantly, the observations do not support a high category, and a certificate is evidence of what a classifier thought about a whole film, not a substitute for the description of it. The right response to a 15 certificate alongside three mild events is to ask what is missing from the event list - which is exactly what the not_stated list flags - rather than to classify upwards on the certificate's authority. Hours, as an independent pass. Service type is given as free_to_air, which resolves the French service branch cleanly. On the provisional category the hours axis is EMPTY: FR-SCH-001 leaves category II timing to the editor's discretion and imposes a placement restriction instead. At category I there is no restriction at all [FR-CLS-001]. I have also listed the category III branch [FR-SCH-002, FR-SCH-004] so the consequence of a higher classification is visible, and recorded that category IV and V are not reached. There is no technical-measure column to fill, and nothing to unlock: on this free-to-air service the only locking regime, category V's, would come paired with a total prohibition rather than a permission [FR-CV-003]. Restrictions, as a third pass, and in France this is where the real burden sits. If the category is II, the pictogram must be on screen for the whole duration of the programme [FR-SIG-001], a written mention must appear with the category II wording [FR-SIG-002], and the classification must be made known at broadcast, in trailers and in press schedules [FR-SIG-003]. None of these has any UK analogue, and a pipeline built on the UK's watershed-and-information model will not look for an on-screen pictogram at all. The placement rule [FR-SCH-001] is the other live obligation, and it cannot be verified: the observations say nothing about surrounding programming, so whether the asset would sit within or near children's programmes is unknown. Checked against the hours: nothing here is a substitute for an hour, because there is no hour. The signage and placement obligations are the compliance measure in their own right, which is the structural difference from the UK on the same asset. Finally, the French slice is strikingly thin for this content. There is no rule in it about sexual dialogue or language, none about nudity, and none about offence or humiliation - so o1 has to be routed through the general 'liable to shock under-10s' test, and o2 and o3 have no French rule at all. Those gaps are recorded, and they are the reason the French confidence is low even though the French answer is the more permissive one.
review_reasons: The classification is unresolved between I (tous publics) and II (-10), and that step is the whole decision: category I carries no pictogram and no obligations, category II carries the full signage regime, and neither carries a clock restriction. FR-CLS-001 is bright_line but its application here is not, FR-CLS-002 is judgment_based, and in France the determination belongs to the editor's own commission de visionnage, which has not made it.

No rule in the French slice addresses sexual dialogue or language. o1 - the observation driving the category - has to be routed through the general 'certain scenes liable to shock minors under 10' test rather than a rule written for it. The UK slice has a rule directly on the discussion of sexual behaviour [UK-SEX-004]; the French slice as given has nothing.

o2 (a bare male chest) and o3 (pain played for comedy) match no rule in the French slice at all. France as given has no nudity rule and no offence or humiliation rule, so two of the three observations have nowhere to land. That is a gap in the table, not a French permission.

FR-FLM-001 is judgment_based and pulls in the restrictive direction: French practice is to RAISE the age limit between cinema and television. The certificate on file is a BBFC 15, a foreign certificate whose route into the French decision is undefined by any rule in the slice. A reviewer must decide how much weight it carries, and resist both carrying the UK 15 across unchanged and inflating it.

FR-CLS-003 is judgment_based and marked human_review_required=yes. I have found category III unsupported, and that finding should be confirmed rather than assumed, particularly as its 'liable to disturb under-12s' limb does not require violence.
The placement restriction at category II [FR-SCH-001] is the operative French obligation and cannot be verified: the observations say nothing about the programming around the transmission.

The event list is not stated to be complete, and the not_stated list records that whether any sexual activity, nudity or strong language occurs elsewhere in the asset is unknown. A French category is assigned to the whole work, so an incomplete list is a more fundamental obstacle here than in the UK - a single depicted scene elsewhere could move the category and introduce an hour where there currently is none.
intended_date is 'not_stated', so the FR-SCH-004 derogation could not be assessed if the category were III. The row is conditional and marked human_review_required=yes.

FR-CV-003 is bright_line and marked human_review_required=yes. It is in the decision to make visible that an upward reclassification to V would refuse this free-to-air transmission outright, not move it later.

missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Settles the I/II question, which is the difference between no French obligations at all and a pictogram on screen for the whole programme plus a written mention and press disclosure.

missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: This is the fact most likely to change the answer. A depicted sexual scene elsewhere could move the category to III and introduce a 22:00 hour where there is currently no clock restriction at all.

missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-CLS-002 asks whether CERTAIN SCENES are liable to shock minors under 10. How long the sequence runs and how explicit the terms are both bear directly on that, and the French slice contains no language rule to handle the words separately.

Neither is a clock test and neither can be checked from an asset description.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Without it the only live French restriction can be stated but not verified, so compliance cannot be confirmed even though no hour applies.

missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-CLS-003 records that a cinema -12 interdiction pulls a film into at least category III and that a CNC avertissement means -12 for television. FR-FLM-002's reclassification route turns on twenty years having elapsed since the last visa.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A French interdiction or avertissement would fix a category floor directly and introduce an hour. Its absence leaves the category to be made from the viewing.

missing_information.why_it_matters: Recorded as not stated. The pictogram must be displayed for the WHOLE DURATION of the broadcast [FR-SIG-001] and the written mention has minimum durations [FR-SIG-002], so the signage plan depends on the programme's shape. The proportion the 'sustained' scene occupies of the whole also bears on the category.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Allows the signage obligations to be specified concretely, and gives the 'sustained' description a denominator.

missing_information.why_it_matters: Not needed for the provisional answer, since category II carries no clock restriction - but needed if the category is III, because FR-SCH-002 sets 22:00 and FR-SCH-004's derogation turns on the weekday, public-holiday eves and the school-holiday calendar.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Only matters on the III branch. Recorded so that the branch is not silently closed.

missing_information.why_it_matters: Trailers carry their own obligations [FR-TRL-001, FR-TRL-002]: the pictogram throughout and no scenes likely to offend young viewers.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Adds further decisions, and the trailer content test does not follow from the feature's category.

missing_information.why_it_matters: Recorded as not stated. It is the second limb of FR-PRO-002, which is an absolute prohibition.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Nothing on this description, because nothing is depicted and the material is not pornographic, so the rule fails on its first limb. Listed so the conclusion rests on that limb rather than on an assumption about the second.

missing_information.why_it_matters: The French rules apply to a service under French jurisdiction, and the observations record the service only as 'free-to-air', a delivery type rather than a French channel.
